question.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+{sin}^{2}t\,k$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4},$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$,  the vector ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

 

$$
R(u)=r(\frac{\pi }{4})+u{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(\frac{\pi }{4}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j+{sin}^{2}(\frac{\pi }{4})\,k \\  & =\,i+\,j+\frac{1}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}t)\,k \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j-\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})k \\  & =\,i-\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point 
 where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
R(u)=\,i+\,j+\frac{1}{2}\,k+u(\,i-\,j+\,k),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
